data_output.description: Unchanged data interface from data.py: load(..., include_test_labels=False) and encode(...) provide train, valid, and test tuples of (features, labels, users). Features have exactly five encoded columns in this fixed order: user_id, video_id, tab, hour derived as floor(numeric hourmin / 100), and weekday derived from date with Monday=0 through Sunday=6. Training and validation labels are long_view binary values; test labels are None. All arrays preserve selected source-row order.

model_input.description: Model input remains an int32 feature matrix of shape [rows, 5] from the unchanged encoder. At each epoch boundary trainer calls Model.predict(train_features) once to create frozen_train_scores aligned exactly to canonical training row indices. build_train_pairs consumes these aligned scores plus training labels and user IDs, returning int64 positive and negative row-index arrays for same-user pairwise batches. Validation is the sole checkpoint/early-stopping split, and final archives contain canonical-order row_ids and scores for validation and test.

trainer.objective: Implement the candidate c01 ablation exclusively in train.py: at the start of every training epoch, use the current frozen additive Model to score all training impressions, then construct K=4 same-user pairwise negatives per positive as two hard negatives plus two uniform negatives whenever at least four same-user negatives exist.
required_changes: Modify only train.py. Change build_train_pairs to accept frozen_train_scores in addition to train_features, train_labels, train_users, and rng; do not change data.py, model.py, or config.json.

For each user group, obtain positive indices where train_labels[index] == 1 and negative indices where train_labels[index] == 0. For every positive of a user with at least four negatives, select exactly two hard negatives: the two negative indices with greatest frozen_train_scores, ordered by descending score and then ascending canonical training index to break ties deterministically. Select exactly two uniform negatives without replacement using rng.choice from that user's remaining negatives after removing the two selected hard negatives. Emit one pair for every selected negative, yielding exactly four pairs per positive.

For a user with fewer than four negatives, preserve the parent sampler's availability behavior by emitting each available same-user negative at most once per positive. Allocate hard negatives first as the highest-scoring available negatives up to two using descending frozen_train_scores and ascending index ties; then sample the remaining available negatives uniformly without replacement up to the remaining K=4 capacity. This retains no replacement and uses all available negatives when fewer than four exist.

At the beginning of each epoch, before build_train_pairs and before any model.step call for that epoch, compute frozen_train_scores = model.predict(train_features). Pass these scores to build_train_pairs. Do not recompute hard-negative scores during batches; the scores must remain frozen for the full epoch.

Update both contract-check calls to build_train_pairs so they provide frozen scores generated by the current probe model on the corresponding training feature matrix. The contract-check may continue to make one probe model.step after sampling.
Do not modify config.json. Keep seed, learning rate, L2, batch size, max epochs, patience, and split behavior exactly as configured.
preserve: Keep the additive five-field scorer unchanged: model inputs remain encoded user_id, video_id, tab, derived hour from hourmin as floor(numeric hourmin / 100) constrained to 0..23, and derived weekday from date as Monday=0 through Sunday=6.
Keep LABEL long_view, the pairwise logistic loss, Adam-style optimizer behavior, L2 regularization, batch shuffling, and all configured hyperparameters unchanged.
Use training labels only for training-pair membership. Do not load, inspect, or infer test labels; retain include_test_labels=False and assert test_labels is None.
Retain validation-only checkpoint selection and early stopping based on valid_primary, computed from validation predictions only.

Retain canonical validation and test prediction archive behavior: the fixed training command must write predictions_valid.npz and predictions_test.npz beside the requested output path, each containing exactly row_ids=np.arange(split_length, dtype=np.int64) and scores=model.predict(split_features) in canonical encoded split row order.
Keep same-user pairing, binary label interpretation, K=4 maximum negatives per positive, and no-replacement sampling behavior.
coordination_notes: Interface contract: data.py remains unchanged and encode(splits) supplies train_features as int32 shape [N,5], train_labels as float32 binary labels, and train_users in canonical training row order; trainer must use those exact arrays and must not introduce source fields or aliases.

Interface contract: Model.predict(features) returns one finite score per input row in the same row order; trainer uses only model.predict(train_features) at epoch start as the frozen hard-negative ranking source.
Hard-negative ranking is training-only and is based on the current model state at the epoch boundary. It is not derived from validation scores, validation labels, test features, or test labels.
No coordination changes are needed from feature_engineer or model_designer because this is a training sampler-only ablation.

reasoning: The parent experiment already uses the required additive five-field scorer and K=4 same-user pairwise objective. The requested ablation changes only which same-user negatives enter each epoch's existing pairwise loss. Freezing train-set model scores at the epoch boundary makes high-score negative selection deterministic conditional on the epoch model and avoids any validation or test influence. Selecting two score-ranked negatives and two uniformly sampled remaining negatives gives the specified 50/50 hard/uniform composition whenever K=4 is feasible, while preserving the parent behavior of using all available negatives for smaller user-negative pools.
